paper_title: A machine learning and centrifugal microfluidics platform for bedside prediction of sepsis (Sepset signature, PREDICT platform)
prediction_task: Binary prediction of clinical deterioration (SOFA worsening >=2) within 24 h in ED/ICU patients with suspected sepsis from a 6-gene transcriptomic signature plus 2 housekeeping genes, deployed via on-chip ddPCR

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Outcome definition confounds prognosis vs diagnosis: SOFA >=2 is prognostic of organ dysfunction, not of infection; pre-Sepsis-3 cohorts split 'sepsis' vs 'severe sepsis' where severe is now the Sepsis-3 sepsis, creating label inconsistency across cohorts.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified SOFA>=2 is Sepsis-3 operational definition (old 'severe sepsis' = current 'sepsis'); edited manuscript to state score used 'to discriminate sepsis from non-sepsis'; distinguished diagnosis vs prognostication concepts.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: AUROC 0.69 and NPV 67% in ED setting deemed effectively a negative result: cannot reliably rule out adverse outcomes at true T0, undermining point-of-care value proposition.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Contextualized vs prior tests at ~50% accuracy; argued accuracy rises to ~90% by ICU admission; suggested 6-12 h retest strategy; attributed ED under-performance to early antibiotics preventing progression.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Bacterial/viral infection patients used as non-sepsis controls while sepsis mimickers (cancer, cardiogenic shock, ACS, IBD — 15-18% of suspected-sepsis cohorts) underrepresented, biasing specificity estimates.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Cited Table 1 rows 11-14 testing 3171 mimicker patients with AUCs 0.50-0.53 (chance-level), framing as desired specificity against non-sepsis; reinforced SOFA>=2 correlation anchors predictions.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Derivation/validation cohorts smaller than claimed; no prospective power analysis presented per setting; refitting six-gene signature across ED vs ICU vs multi-country cohorts risks tuning leakage.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Supplied DeLong-based power calc (n=376 for 90% power vs PCT); n=586 used in derivation; asserted ddPCR results consistent with RNA-seq across follow-on cohorts in Table 1 bottom rows.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Independence of 15 'external' test datasets questioned — reviewer asked explicitly whether signatures were ever tuned/refit on these cohorts, with limited detail on RNA extraction and HKG stability across populations.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Listed 2 training sets + 9 sepsis test cohorts + 6 non-sepsis test cohorts; showed automated vs manual RNA extraction gave similar Ct (delta Ct <1); HKGs PTP4A2 and CHTOP selected for low variance across 2,833-candidate screen.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Pathophysiological link between the 6-gene immunosuppression/reprogramming signature and SOFA-defined deterioration requires deeper mechanistic discussion; over-reach in claiming test replaces other clinical variables.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added mechanistic paragraph linking positive SepsetER to dysfunctional host response; softened claim that 'no other information should be needed' by adding 'although other clinical predictors could complement this test.'
